classification.habitat: Cultivated fields and cool-season agricultural land
classification.distribution: Widely cultivated in India and other temperate to subtropical regions

identification.description: Small erect annual herb with trifoliate leaves, pale flowers and characteristic angular yellow-brown seeds.
identification.whole_plant: Annual herb, generally erect and branched, with a distinctive aromatic odour.
identification.stem: Soft, erect to ascending, green and branched.
identification.leaf: Trifoliate; leaflets obovate to oblong, with toothed margins; stipules present.
identification.flower: Small pale yellow to whitish flowers, usually solitary or in small axillary groups.
identification.fruit: Slender curved to sickle-shaped pod containing several seeds.
identification.seed: Hard, angular, yellowish-brown to brown seeds with a characteristic strong odour and bitter taste.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a herbaceous annual.

therapeutics.precautions: Excessive intake may cause gastrointestinal effects; clinical use should follow an appropriate reference.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Fenugreek seeds contain soluble fibre, saponins and amino-acid derivatives; composition varies with cultivar and processing.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Fenugreek has been investigated for glycaemic, lipid, digestive and lactation-related outcomes. Evidence varies by preparation and study design, so this record does not treat these findings as established clinical indications.
modern_information.safety_notes: May affect glucose levels and may interact with medicines; gastrointestinal effects and allergy are possible.

exam_points: Fruit is a slender curved pod
viva_questions: Which family does Methika belong to?
mnemonics: Methika = Methi: three leaflets and angular seeds.
student.quick_revision: Methika (Trigonella foenum-graecum): annual Fabaceae herb; seed is the main useful part; trifoliate leaves and curved pods are key identification features.

teaching_points: Demonstrate trifoliate leaves and seed morphology.
Relate morphology to common kitchen fenugreek while distinguishing medicinal crude-drug quality.
discussion_points: Traditional Deepana/Vatanulomana claims versus modern evidence
practical_points: Examine seed colour, shape, odour and taste safely.
Observe pod and leaf characters on fresh material.

doctor.quick_reference: Methika is traditionally used mainly as seed in digestive and selected metabolic contexts; dosing is intentionally not supplied without a verified reference.
key_precautions: Potential glucose-lowering effect may be relevant with antidiabetic medicines
